::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: convex-at-hessian-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The graph of f(x) = x^3 for x from -1.2 to 1.2, flat at the origin.
#|   A dashed vermilion chord joins (-1, -1) and (0.5, 0.125) and passes
#|   through (0, -0.25), below the graph's value 0 at x = 0.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
ch_x_ch <- seq(-1.2, 1.2, length.out = 241)
ch_graph_ch <- tibble::tibble(x = ch_x_ch, f = ch_x_ch^3)
ch_ends_ch <- c(-1, 0.5)
ch_chord_ch <- tibble::tibble(x = ch_ends_ch, f = ch_ends_ch^3)
ch_mid_x_ch <- c(0, 0)
ch_mid_f_ch <- c(-0.25, 0)
ch_mid_ch <- tibble::tibble(x = ch_mid_x_ch, f = ch_mid_f_ch)
ch_mid_cols_ch <- c("#D55E00", "#0072B2")
ch_graph_ch |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = f) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = ch_chord_ch, colour = "#D55E00", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = ch_chord_ch, colour = "#D55E00", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = ch_mid_ch, colour = ch_mid_cols_ch, size = 2) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = "f(x)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: convex-at-hessian-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The graph of f(x) = x^3 for x from -1.2 to 1.2, flat at the origin.
#|   A dashed vermilion chord joins (-1, -1) and (0.5, 0.125) and passes
#|   through (0, -0.25), below the graph's value 0 at x = 0.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

ch_x_py = np.linspace(-1.2, 1.2, 241)
ch_ends_py = np.array([-1, 0.5])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))
ax.plot(ch_x_py, ch_x_py**3, color="#0072B2")
ax.plot(ch_ends_py, ch_ends_py**3, "--o", color="#D55E00", markersize=4)
ax.plot([0], [-0.25], "o", color="#D55E00", markersize=4)
ax.plot([0], [0], "o", color="#0072B2", markersize=4)
ax.set_xlabel("x")
ax.set_ylabel("f(x)")
plt.show();
```

:::

The [graph](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-graph) of $f(x) = x^3$ from @exm-convex-at-hessian, with $\smallconst = 1$.
Above $x = 0$, the dashed [chord](algebra-sums.qmd#def-chord) from $-1$ to $\tfrac{1}{2}$ is at height $-\tfrac{1}{4}$,
which is below $f(0) = 0$,
although $f''(0) = 0$.

:::
